Photoreal cinematic live-action, 1881 London, 35 mm film grain, natural weight and pace.
[Shot 1] From 00:00 to 00:06. The shot begins from <Picture 2>: a medium shot of the rock ledge above the boulder: three turkey vultures settled along it in a row, blackish-brown plumage hunched and wings folded, each bare red head turned down toward the camera, the steel-blue sky behind them. The camera is on the plateau rock below the ledge, level with a standing man's eye and four long strides from the ledge, an 85mm lens. The white afternoon sun stands high and a little behind the camera. At the first frame Three turkey vultures stand in a row across the CENTRE of frame at half the frame height on a grey rock ledge with blackish-brown plumage and bare red heads turned down, the grey rock of the ledge runs to both edges at the BOTTOM, and steel-blue sky fills the TOP. The camera pushes in on the birds across the whole shot, travelling a long stride as the nearest bird's bare red head turns further down toward the camera, from 00:00 to 00:03. At 00:03 the wind lifts the ragged feathers along its folded wing, and the lift continues to the last frame of the shot.
